1790 - The rebellion

The sky was orange, lit up by the dozens of canons going off. Pirates everywhere, killing and plundering. About twenty years earlier, it was struck by a drought and then a large frost. The people had risen to a rebellion, splitting the islands into ten territories. The most powerful of them were the Chumimin, which were ruthless pirates. The Ninuki, which was considered the only place of order, and the Xings, which were constantly trying to unite the mass of islands with no success. The whole Isle was known as the Isle of Death due to the immense amount of pirates and dangerous reefs surrounding the large cluster of islands. During that time, the people of the islands were under constant raid by the Pirates. But the people devised a police force by stealing pirate ships and using them to protect citizens. Unfortunately, the massive drug empire that the pirates were built upon made the citizens' protection very corrupt, very fast. This turned out to be a problem when villages and towns were being raided. Anyone who tried to question the authority of the citizens protection was considered a criminal and executed. This made the villagers lose all hope, since there was no one to protect them from the pirates and bandits. 

Soon enough, the pirates had established one of the most functioning statocracies in Erene. A stratocracy is a nation whose government IS the military, just so you know. They called themselves Kakaminikaku, which means The land of ships. It was every trade ships worst nightmare. This turned out to be a problem for the people, because since no one wanted to trade with them, they had no resources and technological advances. So the Kakaminikaku devised a plan. The male population were forced to do military exercises at the age of fifteen. The female population was split into three classes of equal rank but different purposes. One class was called the Repuks which means Maintenance people. These people usually worked on repairing boats and buildings (as suggested by the name) The second class was called the Medinia which means Doctors or Nurses. There were typically about two of these women working on ships. Their work included everything injury related as the pirates said. The third class was the most important of them all. The Resonu which means metal collectors. These people were miners, and were the women responsible for hard work in the mines, whose only use was to collect metals for the Kakaminikaku. This was a severe issue, since without technological safety, poor education, and only women working there, the fatality rate was a large 35%. That is why the population of the Kakaminikaku was so low.

1830 - provocation of the Arenenett fleet.

	In 1828, a group of people called the Nanor rose up secretly within a small island south of most of them. They heard stories from their grandparents about the possibility of another nation being south-west of that island. The Nanor said it was the only way to freedom. They took months to make a plan of action, but finally they did it. They decided they would steal a military patrol boat from a pirate that came to the island to check on the citizens. The patrol boat would have sailed for three days to get to the north island to give them the status of citizens. If he was late, it would take another three days to get down there. After the Nanor would steal the boat, they would sail to that nation south of them, and try to get them to liberate all of the islands. 

About three days later, a patrol boat at the south island was stolen. The first part of the plan was executed perfectly without them knowing. The Nanor was sailing, when a canon whizzed past them. They were being followed by the Kakaminikaku. It turns out that there are info stations all around the island, and they were fast to detect that something was wrong. The Nanor was in trouble. If they didn't make it, the isles would be enslaved until another nation finds them. They needed to steer out of the pirates aim. Hours of steering, fighting, and hoping later and the pirates were closer to the Nanor than ever. In the midst of the fighting, the Nanor saw land in the distance. The crew felt true hope, hope that they could be saved. Sometime later, the Nanor also saw ships in the distance. Warships. This nation saw them, and alerted their navy. As the warships approached, the crew and its attackers became confused. Suddenly, they stopped attacking each other. As the Nations Ships came closer, they became visible to detail. It was like the ships were made of metal. A metal boat was thought to be impossible, as the metal was heavier than the water. But alas, science came into play. Metal warships were coming to them. When the metal warships finally approached the Nanor and the pirates, they had a brief staredown. Then finally, the metal boats said something in a foreign language, You are on Arenese waters. Please turn around or be sunken. You have no authority here, and must leave immediately. The myth was true. This isn't just another island ruled by the Kakaminikaku. This is a whole nation with impossible technology. The Nanor with haste raised a completely white flag, which was a flag of yield. We accept your surrender. Now turn around and go back to where you came from. But the Nanor slowly crept forward. The crew all on the poop deck (yes thats the word) with their hands completely raised. Including the captain. One of the metal ships went up to the Nanor and their crew came out with ready muskets. The boat then proceeded to board the Nanors ship with caution. The captain of that metal ship said in a foreign language Who are you; why are you here? The Nanor stood still, not uttering a word. The captain slowly raised his shirt to reveal a starving body with many bruises and scars. The metal boats crew then understood what was happening and then decided to take them to shore. They tied them up and started to walk back to their boat. Just as they did that, a canon pierced the floor infront of them. The pirates were still there watching, and started to yell. Immediately, the foreign navy started to fire at the pirate boats. The Nanor were scared and quickly gave many signs of surrendering. The foreign crew on the stolen boat understood what was happening, and hurried to the metal boat. The Nanor followed them into the inside cabin, where they were locked in until the fight was over.

The foreign navy seemed invincible. When the canons hit their boat, minimal damage was sustained. The boat also fired at an impossible speed. The pirates were decimated in less than one hour, with the only damage that they did to the foreign navy being a large dent. The foreign navy then immediately went back to shore. At shore, they tried to get a translator to translate the words of the Nanor into their language. Fortunately, the language of the Nanor was also the language of the Gwacheons. Quickly the Nanor and the foreign people began to communicate. The name of this foreign nation that saved the Nanor was Arenenge. After many conversations, the Nanor and the Arenese were on equal terms. The Arenese navy immediately began getting their navy ready and warning other nations about this Kakaminikaku. After many years of preparation, they were ready for war.

1837 - The war of the East Isles

	One of the first fully metal warship squadrons and the rest of Arenenges navy was sent out to take care of the Kakaminikaku Stratocacy. The first contact of the Arenenge navy to the Pirates was midday, about a day after their declaration of war. The metal squad fired first, and the Pirates were struck and unorganized, they were confused as they scrambled to their stations, delaying their response. By then the attack was almost over. But the Pirates still tried to stay alive. They did every tactic possible, but did not prevail. The pirates lost badly, and that was just one encounter with the Pirates. Hundreds of more like this came; no time to get to their stations and protect themselves. Soon the Pirates noticed what was happening, and alerted the entire state. Soon the Kakaminikaku were in full force, as they mobilized every single boat and human they had, as well as tried to call for help. Unfortunately, their pride was the death of them. The Arenese navy was not only more technologically advanced, but had more supplies and preparation. Soon, the Arenese navy had pushed the Pirates quite far, and had completely liberated three very large islands from the Kakaminikaku State. So far, it had been three years, with many ships having to go to the mainland to refill supplies. Everything was going perfectly. The pirates were definitely putting up a fight, but the Arenese Navy had not yet seen the bloodiest day of their life. April 17, 1839 was the day of blood, as the event was called. The Arenese navy landed on Kakaminikakus most populated island, and there they planned to make the Kakaminikaku surrender. 37,000 troops landed on the Island of Undikash. When they first landed, it was quiet. Far too quiet for them. They advanced a few yards, and into the forest. After a couple hours of nothing, they finally came upon the city of Chaancog. The marines cleared house after house, then met in the center, where they saw a single man burning while being crucified. The squadron immediately went in a house, where they were met by a citizen. It turns out these citizens were undercover pirates, and violently ambushed many of the marines. The marines did not have enough time to react, and many of them died. The next squadron of Marines tried to flank through the west forest, but were met with poison arrows and explosives. These two acts alone was enough to measure a small war. Two surviving marines retreated back to the shore, where they met with the rest of the squadrons. They had to plan this out.

	After many hours of planning, it was getting night. The  Marines decided to camp off of the shore, after clearing out a small portion of the forest. They set up small posts, traps to ensure no enemy could get to them without waking up. Most soldiers went to sleep, though some stayed awake and woke up others when they got too tired. They survived the night, and in the morning they were ready for another round.That morning, they woke up to yelling. It was about 4:30AM, but the officers could not resist yelling. When they opened their eyes, they saw thousands of men running to them holding knives and swords. Everyone woke up and immediately got to their muskets to shoot the Pirates. But it wasn't enough, the speed of reloading a single shot musket was far too slow, and the thousands had reached the camp. Just then, someone finally manned the warships and started shooting away at the horde. The soldiers on the ground picked up their bayonets and swords and then started to fight the Pirates in hand to hand combat. Some pirates had stolen the muskets and flintlocks of the dead Marines and learned how to use them. The pirates were surprisingly accurate in their aim, so they were just worse to deal with. The one thousand crewmen in the navy near the shore saw the fighting and came to help. They started blasting away at the Pirates, but accidentally hit some friendly marines in the process. They decided it would be better if they came closer to shore, since the canons were not yet accurate enough to shoot such a small target from afar. When the ships moved in, the Pirates got very weary. Some pirates started to go crazy, and pushed through the main of the muskets. Other Pirates killed some of their own team, and even themselves. Bodies piled up along the shoreline, and thousands of casualties were reported from both sides. Finally, the remaining Pirate group retreated into the forest, but not before they were chased down by the marines. The Marines and Army swept the rest of the Island for the next three days, coming into more battles, and barely surviving. Then, they finally reached the Capitol building, where only the most elite pirates were. When the army charged inside through the front gates, they were met with corpses. Both men and women, gushing blood everywhere. It was a horrifying scene for everyone there. The Pirates had killed themselves off for good. Only two islands remained, which were quickly captured. 

1840 - The annexation of the East Isles

	 Six months later, about a year after the new president was elected, Arenenge decided to help the people of the islands rebuild, so they made a peace treaty that said This land will be fully annexed into Arenenge, but fifty years later, in the year 1890, this land will be given back to the peoples of Nanor. They decided to name the land Nanor after the brave group who alerted the Arenese navy of the pirates and their evil regime. The new land was given much money, and international support. Many buildings were rebuilt to fit modern standards, new schools were in place, trade was established, culture thrived, and much more. The islands were nicknamed Kakaminzu which meant Land of Culture. Thousands of more people were being saved, as they did not have to work as hard, and modern medicines were put in place. Many people were being fed, and a lot of thanks were given. Over the years, Nanor was steadily reconstructing itself, and by 1890, it was ready to separate from Arenenge. When the people received word, they disagreed and thought the islands should stay in Arenenge, because it would collapse without it. They argued, and protested, and even rioted in some places. The current president of Arenenge finally passed a bill that would keep Nanor in Arenenge. Later, Nanor was split up between five administrative states, and each state had different power than the mainland states, being able to build their national guard, and investigate things more freely than the mainland states. The five states to this day live in harmony together, and never once tried to break away.

	1910 - Mass tourism

	About twenty years later, the five states released limitations on traveling, and when people heard about this, many people visited or moved to the islands. It is estimated that five million people moved or visited within the first six months of opening, and the economy then was booming. Most hotels were completely full, and some took advantage of this and raised their prices. Some people began making their houses rentable, and made much money because of this. The tourists didn't just come from Arenenge, but they were from all over the place. Some people have nicknamed it Kakamishinzu which means Land of many people, for there were many different people with different cultures, nationalities, and ethnic groups moving in. With all of this tourism, it made Arenenges GDP even bigger than it was before. The Arenett government created the Department of External Revenue or D. E. R. This department helped with revenue coming from different nations. Because what happens is people turn a different currency into Arenenges Mints when visiting to pay for stuff. They do this by going to an office or service. This was a problem because offices would often be filled or unavailable, and after the day the offices had no money left. The D. E. R. helped with this by assigning people to different offices, giving offices more money, implementing a tax for changing into Mints, ETC. This didn't seem to upset people, and made Arenenges GDP shoot up even higher. Today, the government expects another tourism surge just like 1910, because of the many new assets the islands have gained; like the newly built Kakaminzu museum, and Ennial Tower. 

1910 - Arenenges rise to the top

The Islands have also helped Arenenge grow in not just its economy, but in its military. Following the naval attack of 1909, Arenenge started to expand its navy to cover all of Nanor with no thinning. The Navy created the foundation of the modern navy that Arenenge has now, as the blueprints used in the first attempt to expand were also borrowed to use in modern battleships, missile cruisers, and destroyers. During the military expansion that started in 1910, the Arenese government began looking to nations with a bigger Navy, such as the British Republic of Bob, gendarme, and United Lativan Republics. They all devised a plan to give Arenenge a stronger nation without the need to directly help them. They decided to give Arenenge three Engineering teams, and one overseer each. This definitely helped Arenenge, as the engineers began to spread knowledge about ships, their experience, what to do, and what not to do. During the expansion in 1912, the Arenett military started to rehaul the Marine Corps. They began by re-doing Marine rankings, starting with the Infantry all the way to the NCO. After this, they began working on the actual exercises, bringing them much more effective training then just useless training. This improved the marines ability to do things by 120%, which stunned the overseers and commanders. After the exercises were sorted out, the actual ships were focused on. More armour was put on, different guns were made, different layout, more efficient engines, and more comfortable bedding and seating. Yes, the islands did all of this. The islands inspired the navy to make perhaps the most important change to their military in all of Arenenges history. Soon, with all of these upgrades, Arenenge became a power in naval, and economical aspects.

2000< - Todays importance

In the end, about 45,000 men, women, and unfortunately children were killed. To this day, this war was the bloodiest in Arenenges history. This war reminds us of the sacrifices anyone would do to save people from horrible death. This also reminds us that we can never lose hope, even when all seems to be lost. The war is one of the most influential in all of Arenenge, because of the sheer stories that were passed down from generation to generation. The islands themselves also serve as a very important trade route for Aramalo, with an estimated 30,000 ships passing through the islands every year. The islands structure tells us a story of not just the war, but before the rebellion. A nation of gold and silver that was not prepared for the storm. A large empire that stretched many miles and captured many nations. A safe haven for everyone. The islands contribution to Erene has not only made it famous, but has made it special. That is why Arenenge strives to keep these lands protected at all costs. The Kakaku Foundation helps Arenenge do that by giving the islands contributions, land, people, food, and more. They are responsible for rebuilding the Ennial Tower after the building accident in 2013.

The islands have also given us rich history. On the island of Nishizi, there lay a pillar made of sandstone, mud, and what seems to be a very similar material to concrete. The pillar was made in three layers, with the very bottom being the largest, and the highest one being the smallest. The bottom layer has a very thin layer of paint in the shape of an elephant, a man, a lion, and a cat. This forms a pattern as these four things cover the entirety of the bottom layer. This layer is ten feet high, with a slight green hue going up (Which is just believed to be moss.) The next layer of the temple is also ten feet high, but this time is a yellowish color. The second layer has carvings that line the exterior walls with a red inside. Though, digging into the second layer does not reveal a red inside, meaning they painted the carvings on the inside. Further examination of the carvings reveal multiple layers of the same four colors: Blue, red, yellow, and purple. Archeologists don't know how all of this was painted, as there is no system or way to get up to that height. They think the way that the people got up was by building a temporary structure to climb. This idea is not strongly supported, as there are no traces of brick, wood, or any building material on the ground. The reason they would paint this is unknown, as throughout history, there was only a scarce amount of attacks, or earthquakes. But recently, Archeologists have discovered not one, but two layers below it. Starting in 1947, an archeologist by the name of Erni K Larin and his team of five people were sent out to the site to attempt to dig up any possible items. Where Erni started was next to the floor layer of the temple, as he thought there someone could have possibly set up something like a tent or market. He didn't even dig 12 feet when he ran into another layer of the pillar. After Erni gathered his thoughts, he called the whole team and told them of his findings. After the team came with bigger tools, they began work. They ended up uncovering 25 feet of new findings. Archeologists are still wondering why this temple exists but some archeologists suggest that this used to be a city, but a large mudslide covered it all. This is strongly supported because of the many small statues, vases, and decorations uncovered in the mud.

Groups of Wonnia

During the 1890s and 1900s there was a group called the Nashkuni. The Nashkuni was a hostile terrorist group aimed to restore the Kakaminikaku. During the peace treaty, this group claimed half of an island to settle, and create a fully independent state named Wonnic Stratocracy. The group also announced their resignation in terrorist activities, as well as hostile attacks. This state became the sole descendant of the Kakaminikaku Stratocracy, and because of this many people despise it. Many ambassadors and diplomats have visited this nation, and reported that it is not as bad as it was previously. Men and women both have equal rights, no more social classes, better economy to support safe environments, and even free speech. Because of this, the Arenese government does not care what it does, as long as it does not directly become the Kakaminikaku Stratocracy. 

	Another independent state that came out of the peace treaty was the Federal Republic of Wonnia. This group claimed the west part of the same island that the Wonnic Stratocracy took. The FRW wants to unite the islands, but under a federal republic. Its first attempt to unite the islands was in 1933, when the president Woodman Willsome sent request to the Arenett government. It got denied for obvious reasons, but ever since, the Federal Republic of Wonnia tries its best to hold on tight to the Kaku culture. At times, the FRW tries to provoke WS, with no success. Unlike the WS, they were never considered a terrorist force, and even participated in anti-terrorist activity between 1910-1938. The FRW is considered the favorite between the two, as they have more rights and freedom, but are generally nicer and cool. [/spoiler][/quote]
